title: GridView media rights register
description: The publication gate's input. One record per media asset that may be processed and published. Absence of a record is itself a refusal: the gate fails closed, so an asset with no entry here can never be processed, uploaded or referenced from a manifest. This file records the *existence* of a permission, never its evidence: no contract, credential or confidential document belongs here, only a reference to where the signed record is held.

status.description: `authoritative` is the real approved inventory that production publication reads. `mock`/`development` mark non-authoritative data. An authoritative inventory with no assets is valid and is the honest state until real approvals exist.

assetId.description: The MediaAsset id this record authorises.

entityType.description: Only the four real owner types. `placeholder` and `unknown` are descriptors, not owners, and nothing owning nothing is publishable.

version.description: Immutable version token, e.g. `v1`. Part of every object key: republishing different content requires a new version rather than an overwrite.

sourceFile.description: Path to the source master, relative to the inventory file. The master itself is only committed when GridView owns it outright.

sourceReference.description: Where the master came from, as a reference a human can follow. Not the asset itself and not a credential.

licenceBasis.description: The licence or permission this publication rests on, e.g. an SPDX identifier or a reference to a signed grant held outside the repository.

attribution.description: The exact credit text to display, or null when the licence genuinely requires none. Null with `attributionPlacement` other than `none` is a contradiction the gate rejects.

attributionPlacement.description: Where the licence requires the credit to appear. GridView implements a central acknowledgements screen only, so `adjacent` is not publishable under the current UI model and the gate refuses it rather than quietly treating the central page as sufficient.

territories.description: Where distribution is permitted. `WORLDWIDE`, or ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes.

expiresAt.description: When the permission lapses, or null when it does not. A lapsed permission is refused.

derivativesAllowed.description: Whether resizing and format conversion are permitted. The pipeline always derives, so false means the asset cannot be processed at all.

approvalStatus.description: Only `approved` permits publication. Everything else, including absence, is a refusal.

provenanceNote.description: Who approved this and against what record. A reference, never the confidential document itself.
